lines: {target}? Shorelines change under your feet. I would stay close enough to hear the bell.
If anyone heads for Beach, tell them. Watch the <wavy>tide</wavy>, the turtles, and the drowned at dusk. I will be at the bell.
Sand looks peaceful until it shifts. I'll remember that from near the bell.
Beach is no small story. Running the wrong way is still running.
I will remember Beach as the place where land starts losing to water. I will stay where I can hear the bell.
Beach might look close from the nearest visible shore. Places lie about distance when I am tired.
A map of Beach would help, especially with a large drawing of the nearest visible shore.
I would try not to make the same mistake twice at Beach. A new mistake is no improvement.
Beach sounds like a place where my best idea would arrive shortly after I left.
At Beach, I would keep the slowest traveler beside me. There is a fair chance that traveler is me.
If I could no longer see the nearest visible shore clearly, I would call that a warning.
If I spotted something unusual at Beach, I would point first and move much later.
Treasure at Beach would still be there after I checked the way home. If not, perhaps it had plans.
The moment cold water taking your strength became a problem, I would stop. Obvious things have a habit of escaping me.
I can sound certain at Beach without being certain. The group should know in advance.
I would remember Beach because of waves moving beyond the boat. My ears keep better notes than I do.
If told not to pull something at Beach, I would stand too far away to hear it as a challenge.
I would not trade the last loaf for a souvenir from Beach. Please remind me I said that.
I would choose one keepsake near the nearest visible shore. Then I would forget which pocket held it.
I wonder what Beach smells like. This is not important, but my nose never asks permission.
{target}? Calm water can still go bottomless. I would stay close enough to hear the bell.
If anyone heads for Deep Lukewarm Ocean, tell them. Don't mistake warm waves for safe waves. I will be at the bell.
The color is kind, but the depth is not. I'll remember that from near the bell.
Deep Lukewarm Ocean is no small story. Running the wrong way is still running.
I will remember Deep Lukewarm Ocean as warm water with a long fall under it. I will stay where I can hear the bell.
At Deep Lukewarm Ocean, even village chores sound good. None of them involve a warm current carrying you from the boat.
If the group split at Deep Lukewarm Ocean, I would choose the half containing the person with the map.
My usual mistake is walking while looking elsewhere. Deep Lukewarm Ocean is a bad place for that hobby.
Before leaving for Deep Lukewarm Ocean, I would check twice that I had a boat, doors, and spare food. Then I would ask someone else.
I might bring back a little kelp, as long as taking it caused no trouble.
I have no clever trick for a drowned rising from below. Leaving is a trick I can usually manage.
I would call the boat waiting at the surface a proper meeting point. I would still put up a sign for myself.
I might be wrong about Deep Lukewarm Ocean. I would prefer to be wrong from a safe spot.
If I spotted something unusual at Deep Lukewarm Ocean, I would point first and move much later.
At Deep Lukewarm Ocean, I would keep my hands off anything that clicked, hissed, glowed, or looked offended.
After Deep Lukewarm Ocean, resting on the way home counts too. Stories make home feel closer than it is.
I would rather turn back early than discover the boat waiting at the surface was farther away than it looked.
I remember places by smells I cannot describe. Deep Lukewarm Ocean sounds likely to become one.
At Deep Lukewarm Ocean, I would mark every turn and then mark the marks so I knew they were mine.
I would not let the scenery distract me from a warm current carrying you from the boat.
{target}? Deep water does not care who can swim. I would stay close enough to hear the bell.
If anyone heads for Deep Ocean, tell them. Take a boat and count your air honestly. I will be at the bell.
The horizon looks simple until you are far from land. I'll remember that from near the bell.
Deep Ocean is no small story. Running the wrong way is still running.
I will remember Deep Ocean as open water with no nearby door. I will stay where I can hear the bell.
I would know I reached Deep Ocean when the deep open water below the boat made me forget what I meant to say.
If the air changed around Deep Ocean, I would mention it before everyone blamed my lunch.
I would find the boat waiting at the surface before going farther. I lose directions more often than chalk.
Back home, everyone would ask about the deep open water below the boat. I would somehow begin with what I ate.
I would rather turn back early than discover the boat waiting at the surface was farther away than it looked.
I have no clever trick for a drowned rising from below. Leaving is a trick I can usually manage.
At Deep Ocean, I would keep the slowest traveler beside me. There is a fair chance that traveler is me.
I might be wrong about Deep Ocean. I would prefer to be wrong from a safe spot.
I would not decide that bubbles rising from deep water meant no trouble at Deep Ocean without asking someone else.
I am the sort of person who notices losing sight of the surface one step late. At Deep Ocean, someone else should lead.
After seeing kelp, plain packed dirt might look quite elegant.
I would look closely at kelp without picking up anything I did not understand. Experience taught me that.
A little embarrassment at the boat waiting at the surface is better than a lot of danger farther on.
At Deep Ocean, I would tie everything twice. Loose laces have excellent timing.
Slow steps near kelp sound dull. Dull steps tend to reach home.
{target}? Warm water can still carry teeth. I would stay close enough to hear the bell.
If anyone heads for Lukewarm Ocean, tell them. Sail smart and do not swim too far from wood. I will be at the bell.
The waves look friendly until night. I'll remember that from near the bell.
Lukewarm Ocean is no small story. Running the wrong way is still running.
I will remember Lukewarm Ocean as gentle water with danger below the color. I will stay where I can hear the bell.
I would ask whether the prize was worth walking past a drowned below the surface. That feels like a short discussion.
People may admire kelp. I would first ask whether it was safe to stand on.
I would warn the group about a drowned below the surface, preferably before my voice became a squeak.
On the way back from Lukewarm Ocean, I would follow our marks instead of inventing a better route.
I would find the nearest visible shore before going farther. I lose directions more often than chalk.
For Lukewarm Ocean, I would set out early enough to return while the bell still sounded ordinary.
A snack near the nearest visible shore sounds like a good way to remember where it is.
Traveling alone gives my ideas too much authority. Lukewarm Ocean deserves a group decision.
At Lukewarm Ocean, I would mark every turn and then mark the marks so I knew they were mine.
There are probably answers at Lukewarm Ocean. I would settle for returning with the questions.
I would let whatever was moving settle before choosing a path.

The moment a current carrying you past the boat became a problem, I would stop. Obvious things have a habit of escaping me.
If anyone got separated at Lukewarm Ocean, I would stay near the nearest visible shore and not improve the plan.
If I stumbled around kelp, I would check my boots before blaming the ground.
{target}? Open water moves distance under your feet. I would stay close enough to hear the bell.
If anyone heads for Ocean, tell them. Keep land in mind and a boat under you. I will be at the bell.
Waves make every direction look the same. I'll remember that from near the bell.
Ocean is no small story. Running the wrong way is still running.
I will remember Ocean as water wide enough to make a bell useless. I will stay where I can hear the bell.
When I told the story of Ocean, I would mention cold water taking your strength before the funny part.
Nothing I carried home from Ocean should make the return dangerous.
Would you trust the nearest visible shore in bad weather? I am asking before I decide that I do.
Food would not solve cold water taking your strength, but being hungry might make it worse.
I ask too many questions around strange places. At least questions do not make cold water taking your strength worse.
I would bring news home if a drowned below the surface blocked the route. Quickly and with many hand gestures.
Ocean might change quickly under fog over the water. I would keep the route home clear.
Confidence feels useful until I remember cold water taking your strength. Then I would rather have a careful plan.
A heavy pack is poor company on the return from Ocean.
If anyone got separated at Ocean, I would stay near the nearest visible shore and not improve the plan.
I would remember Ocean because of waves moving beyond the boat. My ears keep better notes than I do.
At Ocean, I would place lights where they pointed home, not where they looked pretty.
I would choose a safe place to rest, then ask whether it was safe. The order needs work.
If Ocean wanted me relaxed, it could move cold water taking your strength somewhere else.
For Ocean, I would pack a boat, doors, and spare food. I would also pack one useless thing and defend it stubbornly.
{target}? A river can carry news or bodies. I would stay close enough to hear the bell.
If anyone heads for River, tell them. Cross where you can see the bottom. I'll be at the bell.
Current makes even shallow water bossy. I'll remember that from near the bell.
River is no small story. Running the wrong way is still running.
I will remember River as moving water that does not wait for anyone. I will stay where I can hear the bell.
Someone should remind me that the familiar bend upstream is for getting home, not just admiring.
I would pay attention to an evening shower. Conditions have a way of winning arguments.
The best part of River could be telling the story from my own bed.
I ask too many questions around strange places. At least questions do not make a current pulling toward deep water worse.
I would know I reached River when the bends in the flowing river made me forget what I meant to say.
I would take breaks at River. When I get tired, every bad idea sounds efficient.
I would eat before reaching River. Hungry me makes decisions that ordinary me questions.
After seeing clay, plain packed dirt might look quite elegant.
I would take a current pulling toward deep water seriously, even if I had just said something very unserious.
Why does clay always sound more harmless than it looks?
At River, if carrying loot made it harder to deal with a current pulling toward deep water, I would leave the loot. I hope.
I can imagine carrying traces of clay home from River.
I would choose one keepsake near the familiar bend upstream. Then I would forget which pocket held it.
I would carry more light to River than seemed necessary. Necessary moves after sunset.
I would borrow confidence from the careful traveler, not the loud one.
{target}? Wet stone is a poor friend to ankles. I would stay close enough to hear the bell.
If anyone heads for Stony Shore, tell them. Step carefully where waves touch rock. I will be at the bell.
Shore rocks make boats complain. I'll remember that from near the bell.
Stony Shore is no small story. Running the wrong way is still running.
I will remember Stony Shore as hard coastline where water sharpens stone. I will stay where I can hear the bell.
I would warn the group about a drowned beyond the shallows, preferably before my voice became a squeak.
I would choose one keepsake near the highest dry ledge. Then I would forget which pocket held it.
I would wait for the careful plan at Stony Shore. Waiting is easier with bread.
If I passed the highest dry ledge twice, I would stop calling it a new landmark.
Maps and I have an agreement. They show the route and I ask a nearby person what it means.
Food would not solve a wave washing over loose rock, but being hungry might make it worse.
If I heard waves knocking stones together, I would listen before deciding it was harmless. That is a new habit.
I would tell the group before stepping away. Waving from far off is not the same thing.
Stony Shore might change quickly under sea fog. I would keep the route home clear.
I would find the highest dry ledge before going farther. I lose directions more often than chalk.
I would ask before moving anything at Stony Shore. Then I would wait for the answer.
Night can have Stony Shore. I would like my bed and the usual ceiling.
A story about Stony Shore needs a safe ending. Otherwise it is a warning with names.
At Stony Shore, I would place lights where they pointed home, not where they looked pretty.
If I forgot why we stopped, I would not assume the reason had gone away.

Coral color does not promise air. I'll remember that from near the bell.
Warm Ocean is no small story. Running the wrong way is still running.
I will remember Warm Ocean as warm waves with danger under the shine. I will stay where I can hear the bell.
Near Warm Ocean, I would miss the bell, my bed, and even the door that sticks.
I would save torches for the return from Warm Ocean. The return always gets the leftovers.

I would choose a safe place to rest, then ask whether it was safe. The order needs work.
At Warm Ocean, nobody needs to prove bravery by ignoring a current carrying you past the reef. Danger does not award prizes.
For Warm Ocean, I would pack a boat, doors, and spare food. I would also pack one useless thing and defend it stubbornly.
At Warm Ocean, I would save food for the return. Future me is forgetful and deserves help.
I would look closely at coral without picking up anything I did not understand. Experience taught me that.
I would number trail marks at Warm Ocean. Somebody else can make sure I do not skip seven.
I would call the nearest visible shore a proper meeting point. I would still put up a sign for myself.
If a souvenir hissed, moved, or glowed too brightly, it could stay at Warm Ocean.
